# SealQL

Start: docs/current-state.md, then docs/llm-integration.md
Substring candidate SQL uses at most three sorted tokens; full proofs and exact predicates are unchanged. This is no result/work limit and changes no public API or stored data; no migration/reindex is needed for this SQL-only update.
Install: npm pack, then install the .tgz; Drizzle >=0.45.2 <0.46, Node >=22.12 or WebCrypto.
Schema/key: examples/standard-consumer.ts; operations: examples/standard-operations.ts
Raw SQL/JOIN: examples/standard-raw.ts; fixed key loading: examples/key-loader.ts
Exports: sealql and sealql/drizzle/v0.45; types in dist/index.d.ts and dist/adapters/drizzle/v0.45/index.d.ts
Security: docs/threat-model.md. Source decisions/evidence are not packaged.
For fixed-format, small-alphabet fields (phone, bank account, resident registration numbers), do not enable substring search; use exact matching only if needed (search: { exact: true }, omit substring), which still leaks equality and frequency.

Purpose: encrypt selected PostgreSQL fields without losing ordinary Drizzle integration. AES-256-GCM binds ciphertext to model/field/scope/row. Standard search uses HMAC candidate tokens plus salted exact/occurrence proofs; PostgreSQL finishes predicates and count, and the app authenticates only returned encrypted projections. Encrypted-only count reads the companion; parent predicates and unfiltered count retain the parent. Count returns one exact number, opens no fields, and rejects results above the safe integer range. No application condition-field verification remains.

Use createSealer with a fixed 32-byte root key (optional fixed model keys), createSealed, field builders, and register(table, { row, scope? }). Export parent and returned companion to drizzle-kit. Installation order: schema migration, every extraMigrationSql statement (functions/statistics/MAIN storage), complete reindex, deploy new queries. Changing profiles requires this same order; partial rebuilds can silently omit rows. No DB version/policy table or key rotation API exists.

Use insert/update/upsert for atomic ciphertext/token/proof writes (undefined means omit). Plain Drizzle encrypted writes raise SEAL_REQUIRED; raw SQL bypasses maintenance. Delete cascades. Await reads before open/openRaw; encrypted projections need registered row/scope properties. UUID and textId rows, text scopes, and scope-free models support kit generate/migrate/repeated push. Never use ordinary Drizzle eq/like/orderBy on encrypted fields.

findMany/count/search support sealed predicates and m.sql. Omitted list limit returns all matches. A required numeric search limit gives the JOIN callback a number limit; omitted or optional caller limits preserve number | undefined. JOIN callbacks must apply where/after/orderBy/limit and select flags or flagsSql; first match table sets order, 1:N requires unique many-side keyset. Condition ciphertext need not be projected. Aliases/self-JOIN are unsupported. Cursors bind scope/match/order (findMany also where), not snapshots; search callback SQL must remain consistent.

Substring minimum is two normalized characters. LIKE supports %, _, and escaped %, _, backslash; every literal run must have at least two normalized characters (ab%cd allowed; ab%z%cd and ab_z raise QUERY_TOO_BROAD). Single-literal LIKE with only edge % wildcards shares positional predicates; whole-value LIKE also checks compact length. General LIKE matches fixed-width segments between % in order; reapply extraMigrationSql for function updates, without reindexing compact-only rows. No respectWords/wordBoundary options or singleton/words proof streams. Exact bits accept 2–32, default16: explicit exact:{bits:2} suits low-cardinality fields without substring indexing; it coarsens candidates, not final equality. exactBitsForPopulation remains unchanged. No encrypted range/sort/aggregation.

List budgets: batch of final matches, fetchBytes/decryptedBytes/resultBytes, deadlineMs, decryptConcurrency. Count budgets: deadlineMs only; signal also supported. maxCandidates was removed. No default work ceiling. Query value/piece keys reach the DB: disable parameter logs in database/driver/proxy/telemetry. Lengths, token frequency, and query observations leak; observed keys recover occurrences. A hostile DB can omit rows or falsify conditions; ciphertext authentication does not authenticate SQL results. 64-bit proof collisions are possible. No full-record theft-resistance claim.

Local Node pg, postgres-js and workerd+pg DB flows were checked. Managed writes/reindex need transactions; transactionless drivers raise UNSUPPORTED_DRIVER. Hosted Cloudflare/Hyperdrive remains unverified.
